payload.query: Design a diversified portfolio across equities, bonds, and commodities for a moderate-risk investor.

payload.analysis: For a moderate-risk investor, we propose a 60% allocation to a global equity index fund, 30% to a mix of high-quality corporate and government bonds with a laddered maturity structure, and 10% to a commodity-focused exchange-traded fund (ETF). This diversification strategy splits risk allocation across asset classes, while maintaining a relatively aggressive growth orientation through equity holdings. Notably, a balanced mix of short- (2-5 year) and intermediate-term (5-10 year) bonds is planned to minimize duration risk. Specifically, we will allocate 60% to the global equity index fund across all buckets and 20% to the commodity ETF across all buckets, while 10% will be devoted to high-quality corporate bonds and 10% to US Treasuries. This portfolio structure should maintain a relatively stable and relatively high returns profile.
